title: Module builder: author a section form with example pre-fill + Health Canada review
walkthrough:
You open a dossier at a module workspace laid out in three columns. The left section tree shows the module title, an always-visible glyph legend ("○ Not started", "◐ In progress", "✓ Complete", "⊘ N/A"), and a list of sections; each row shows a status glyph, the section number and title, an optional "✦AI" badge where AI drafting is available, and a "req"/"opt" badge. A collapsed "Not required for this generic (N)" details block holds the N/A sections.

The right rail leads with a submission tower and a module card: a progress bar, an "X/Y required sections complete" count, and readiness flags "○ Documents · ○ Fee · ○ Valid eCTD". If any sample/AI drafts are unconfirmed, a red "⚠ N sample/AI draft value(s) remain" banner sits here and is never collapsed. Below, the "Draft completeness check" (ValidationCard) stays expanded; the secondary panels — "Submission lifecycle & deficiency clock", "eCTD sequences & package export", "Bilingual / XML Product Monograph detail", and "Collaboration & task assignments" — are each collapsed behind a one-line "Show details" expander (the sequences one force-opens if export is blocked).

Selecting a section shows the center panel: an eyebrow reading module, section number and applicability (e.g. "Module 1 · Section 1.2.2 · required"), the title, its purpose, and a "What Health Canada needs here" teach box with the guidance. The format/bilingual/source reference now sits behind a collapsed "Format & source" expander; a collapsed "eCTD in plain language" primer (leaf, sequence, working vs active, new/replace/append/delete) is also available. An action bar offers "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app", and "⊘ Mark N/A".

Choosing "✦ Author in-app" opens a form (for AI-eligible sections a mode toggle "💬 Draft with AI" / "✦ Fill the form" appears first). A note explains it produces a PDF/A leaf at its eCTD position (lifecycle operation: new), that known facts are pre-filled, and that fields marked "example — replace this" show greyed example text you must replace. Fields carry regulatory labels like "Canadian Reference Product (brand)", "s.5 statement (per patent)", "AUC 90% CI"; sample fields are empty with a greyed "e.g. …" placeholder and an "example — replace this" tag. You edit them, then click an "Author …" button ending in the section title ("Authoring…" while busy), or run "Review vs Health Canada" first.

A review panel then reads "Health Canada review:" followed by "no blocking content gaps." on pass, or "N to fix, M to check." with a bulleted list, each carrying a suggested edit and an "HC guidance ↗" link. The saved document card shows the filename, size, "fingerprint md5" fragment, a provenance chip, and "Download". While the draft holds example values or is an AI draft, a persistent red banner reads "⚠ Not yet filable — review required." — a sample draft clears once no example values remain (server-detected); an AI draft needs the button "I have reviewed this AI draft — it is my content".

The completeness check names the profile and version on its face, with the qualifier "(structural; not HC eValidator)", a disclaimer, and buttons "What this does / does NOT check" and "Rule catalogue (CA-E/CA-W ids)". A collapsed "Technical check & report" expander holds a PDF header/encryption sub-check and CSV/JSON export, with a footnote: this is a presence/format check, not a Health Canada review and not full eCTD validation. The right-rail progress and tree glyph update on completion.
